about_preview.label: About
about_preview.title: Greg Mittelette
about_preview.quote_translation: We don't learn for school, but for life.
about_preview.text: Over 1,100 students mentored. 80% admitted to a top 30 global university or grande ecole. Our edge: we know the final destination (Stanford, Polytechnique, EPFL), which lets us build the right path from day one.

q1.question: What commitment does this require from the family?
q1.answer: Serious mentoring is teamwork. We expect consistency in sessions, transparency on transcripts and goals, and real parent involvement in orientation decisions. In return, we commit to personalized follow-up and genuine availability between sessions.

q2.question: When should we start?
q2.answer: The earlier, the better. Ideally 6th-7th grade: we build the math foundations, choose the right curriculum, anticipate the key transitions. But we also work with students who come in during 11th or 12th grade : the work is different, more intensive, but the results are there.

q3.question: How many students do you take on?
q3.answer: Few. We follow each student personally, sometimes over several years. It's not a scalable model and that's by design. If we're full, we'll tell you : we'd rather say no than do it halfway.

q4.question: What does the process look like?
q4.answer: We start with a diagnostic: current level, ambitions, target schools. From there we propose a work plan. Sessions are weekly, in person or via video. We check in regularly with parents and adjust based on results and deadlines.

q5.question: Do you work with families abroad?
q5.answer: Most of our clients are expats or between two countries. We work via video with families in Dubai, Singapore, London, New York. French system, AEFE schools, IB, BFI : we know these curricula and more importantly, how they translate in admissions files.

about.title: The Founder
about.subtitle: "Non scholae, sed vitae discimus" – Seneca
about.bio_text1: Centrale Lyon for engineering, ISTIA for organization, MIT X for supply chain analytics. I saw from the inside how admissions actually work. Who gets in, who doesn't, and why.
about.bio_text2: The most invested families are often the most misguided. They pay for tutoring, stack extracurriculars, hope the grades will speak for themselves. Meanwhile, the spots go to those who understood the rules of the game.
about.bio_text3: For 14 years, I've been bridging those two worlds. From 6th grade to the gates of Stanford, Polytechnique, EPFL. By building a strategy: which curriculum, which timeline, which positioning, so that on decision day, the application leaves no doubt.
about.bio_text4: 1,100 students. The reality hasn't changed: when you know where you're going, every decision becomes obvious.
about.philosophy_text1: I take on few students. That's a choice. Because my job is to know each one of them : their transcripts, their strengths, what they hide, what holds them back.
about.philosophy_text2: I follow them over the long run. Sometimes from 6th grade to the moment they open the letter. When I build an application for Stanford, Oxford or Ginette, I'm not taking a guess : I know what separates a yes from a no.
about.philosophy_text3: I live internationally, like most of my clients. We understand each other because we share the same reality: an ambition for our children, opaque systems, and the refusal to leave it to chance.
about.philosophy_text4: Today, I'm preparing my own children, aged 9 and 11, exactly the way I prepare my students. Same rigor, same vision. That's the most honest proof of what I believe in.

schools.subtitle: Jeannine Manuel, École alsacienne, Franklin, Stanislas, Swiss boarding schools: we prepare your child's entry into the school that suits them, from primary to high school.
schools.intro_text: A university admission is prepared years in advance, and it often starts with the choice of a school. The great Paris schools are not alike: academic demands, pace, the place of English, the way pupils are treated. The right choice depends on your child, not on a ranking. For years we have been working with pupils from Jeannine Manuel, Franklin, École alsacienne and the Lycée international de Saint-Germain: we know what these schools expect, and what really counts at entry.
schools.steps_subtitle: Depending on whether the school is already chosen, and on how much time is left before the application.
schools.step1_desc: School reports, a family questionnaire, three tests taken at home then marked and commented, an interview with your child and one with you. Within three days, a written report: your child's real level, the two or three schools that suit them, and what each one looks at.
schools.step2_desc: The gaps measured against what the school expects, a work plan, practice in the school's own conditions, a mock interview, then the application and the timeline until the answer.
schools.step3_desc: A review of every school report, preparation for the assessment and interview in the months before the deadline, an application reviewed, and the right moment to apply.
schools.rule1: No place is ever promised: we prepare your child, the school decides.
schools.rule2: Two well-chosen schools are worth more than four random applications.
schools.rule3: A school is chosen on the child's real level: that is why everything starts with tests.

tomorrow.meta_title: What future for my child with AI? An action plan built for them | Carmine Admission
tomorrow.meta_description: Careers, school, skills: what should your child learn for the world ahead? An interview, an assessment and a written action plan, built for them. In complete confidence.
tomorrow.h1: What your child should learn now, for the world ahead.
tomorrow.sub: Changing careers, schools slow to adapt, skills everyone talks about: your questions are legitimate. I answer them for your child, with a consultation, an assessment and a written action plan. Then, if you wish, I stay with them over time.
tomorrow.doc_1_d: Who your child is today: results, way of reasoning, what drives them.
tomorrow.doc_2_d: Subject by subject, what is secure and what is missing, from their tests.
tomorrow.doc_3_d: What AI will amplify in them, and what it will make less useful.
tomorrow.doc_4_d: The paths that suit them, without choosing a career on their behalf.
tomorrow.doc_5_d: School, languages, track, country: what to decide, and when.
tomorrow.doc_6_d: This term, this year, the next three years. Who does what.
tomorrow.q_title: The same questions come up, in every family.
tomorrow.q1: Will the career they imagine still exist when they are twenty-five?
tomorrow.q2: Is school teaching them what will really matter?
tomorrow.q3: Should they learn to code, or is that already outdated?
tomorrow.q4: Which abilities should they develop, and at what age?
tomorrow.q5: With AI, do mathematics and writing still matter?
tomorrow.q6: Which school, which track, which country: how do we decide?
tomorrow.q_answer: General answers are everywhere. None of them applies to your child: the right one depends on their actual level, how they reason, what motivates them, and what your family envisions for them. That is the work I do.
tomorrow.c_title: Nobody knows the jobs of 2040. We do know what will prepare for them.
tomorrow.c1_d: Reasoning, writing precisely, calculating, mastering several languages: this is what lets you judge a machine's work. A child who cannot check will depend on the tool.
tomorrow.c2_t: The career is not the right question.
tomorrow.c2_d: No one chooses a career at twelve. You build abilities and achievements that open several doors, and keep the best ones open.
tomorrow.c3_t: AI is learned as a tool.
tomorrow.c3_d: Early, and to go further, never to do the work for them. Used well, it accelerates a good student. Used badly, it stops them from becoming one.
tomorrow.c4_t: The big decisions are made early.
tomorrow.c4_d: School, languages, subjects, country: each choice opens or closes doors, often years before anyone notices.
tomorrow.c_note: This is how the families who prepare their children earliest think. They do not try to guess the future: they decide what is within their control.
tomorrow.how_title: A consultation, an assessment, a plan. Then ongoing guidance, if you wish.
tomorrow.s1_d: One hour, prepared from a questionnaire. Your child, your family, your ambitions, the countries you are considering, what worries you. You leave with answers already.
tomorrow.s2_d: Written tests suited to their age, in mathematics, French, English and reasoning, which I mark myself. Then a conversation with your child, alone. We then know where they truly stand.
tomorrow.s3_d: A written document, which I present to you in a second meeting: their portrait, actual level, direction, the decisions ahead and the timeline. The plan is yours.
tomorrow.s4_d: Regular check-ins with your child and with you, school reports read, the plan adjusted. And my presence at the moments that decide: a change of school, subject choices, applications.
tomorrow.about_p1: An engineer by training, I have taught mathematics and physics for fourteen years, to students in France and around the world.
tomorrow.about_p2: For several years now, international families have entrusted me with far more than lessons: steering their children's education, choosing schools, guiding subject and career choices, and admissions to the most selective universities. I also take part in work on what schools will need to teach tomorrow.
tomorrow.about_p3: I build every plan myself. I do not delegate this work.
tomorrow.frame1_t: A few families at a time
tomorrow.frame1_d: Because every plan is made by me.
tomorrow.frame2_d: No family is ever named. A written agreement on request.
tomorrow.frame4_d: French, international, British or American curriculum.
tomorrow.f1_a: From primary school to the final year of secondary school. Tests and conversation are adapted to the child's age; the earlier we start, the more room the plan has.
tomorrow.f2_q: Should my child prepare for the tests?
tomorrow.f2_a: No. They measure their actual level, they are not a grade. Your child takes them at home, alone, within the time given.
tomorrow.f3_q: How is this different from a careers adviser?
tomorrow.f3_a: The plan starts from your child's actual level, measured by tests I mark, not from a single conversation. And it does not stop at choosing a track: it says what to build, in what order, and when to decide.
tomorrow.f4_a: The fee is given during our first exchange. It depends on your child's age and on what their situation requires.
tomorrow.f5_a: The plan is yours: you can carry it out on your own. If you wish, I stay with you over time.
tomorrow.final_sub: Write me a few lines: their age, their school, what concerns you. I will reply personally.

adults.meta_title: AI scares me: an action plan for you | Carmine Admission
adults.meta_description: Will your job change? Should you learn AI, and what exactly? An action plan built on your situation, by Greg Mittelette.
adults.label: For you
adults.hero_title: AI scares me: where do I start?
adults.hero_subtitle: You worry about your children, and sometimes about yourself: your job, your place, what you ought to learn. I offer parents what I do for their children: look at the situation squarely, and come out with an action plan.
adults.questions_title: Four questions that keep coming back
adults.q1_desc: Rarely all at once. It is tasks that change. Knowing which ones, in your own work, changes the question entirely.
adults.q2_title: Should I learn AI, and what exactly?
adults.q2_desc: Not everything. What serves your work and your plans. A general course is reassuring; targeted learning saves time from the first week.
adults.q3_title: Is it too late to change?
adults.q3_desc: The tools are quick to learn when you start from your own work. What matters is the order in which you take them on.
adults.q4_desc: With an honest inventory: what you do, what AI can already do, what it won't. The rest follows.
adults.vision_title: Fear comes from what we don't look at squarely.
adults.vision_text1: AI doesn't hit everyone the same way. Within the same job, some tasks become faster and others gain value. Most people have never sorted this out for their own work.
adults.vision_text2: Learning AI from your own job is much faster than a general course. That is what I did: as a teacher, I built with it the tools my students use today.
adults.vision_text3: And what you learn also helps your children. A parent who understands AI guides their choices better.
adults.proof_title: I work with AI every day
adults.proof_text1: I have taught mathematics for fourteen years, to more than 1,100 students, and I guide applications to the most selective universities.
adults.proof_text2: I built with AI the tools my students use: Fields, for olympiad problems; Summit, for the SAT; Xiaomo, for Chinese. I won't talk to you about AI from a distance.
adults.step1_desc: Your job, your actual tasks, your skills, your constraints, what you want. A questionnaire, then a conversation.
adults.step2_desc: What AI changes in your work: what is exposed, what gains value, what it won't do.

bilan.meta_title: Academic level and guidance assessment for your child, primary to high school | Carmine Admission
bilan.meta_description: Where does your child really stand, and should you be worried? Level tests, a consultation and a written report: a clear assessment, from primary to high school.
bilan.h1: Where does your child really stand? A clear answer, within days.
bilan.sub: You wonder whether they are at the right level, on the right path, whether AI changes anything for them. The assessment measures their actual level through tests, we meet for a consultation, and you receive a written report on where they stand and what matters now.
bilan.doc_1_d: In mathematics, French, English and reasoning, measured by their tests.
bilan.doc_2_d: What they can build on, including what their grades do not show.
bilan.doc_3_d: The precise gaps, and the ones that really matter for what comes next.
bilan.doc_4_d: A frank answer, without alarm or false reassurance.
bilan.doc_5_d: The three things to do in the coming months, and the decisions ahead.
bilan.q_label: The assessment is for you if
bilan.q_title: You have a precise question, and their grades do not answer it.
bilan.q1: You wonder whether they are truly at their class level, or above it.
bilan.q2: A decision is coming: school, subjects, language, international section.
bilan.q3: Their results are slipping, or do not match what you see of them.
bilan.q4: You are moving country or system, and do not know where they stand.
bilan.q5: You read a lot about AI and the future, and no longer know what to think for them.
bilan.q6: You want a frank outside opinion before committing further.
bilan.q_answer: The assessment answers one question: where do they stand, and what should be done now? It does not build their whole path. That is what the action plan is for.
bilan.how_title: Tests, a consultation, a report. About a week.
bilan.s1_d: Their schooling, their school, what concerns you. Ten minutes, so that tests and conversation are on target.
bilan.s2_d: Mathematics, French, English and reasoning, suited to their age and curriculum. They take them alone, timed, without preparation. I mark and comment on them.
bilan.s3_d: A few minutes with your child, to hear them reason. Then with you: the results, your questions, my answers.
bilan.s4_d: Their level subject by subject, strengths, gaps, and priorities for the coming months. It is yours.
bilan.next_title: The assessment stands on its own.
bilan.next_text: Many families stop there, with a clear answer. If you want to go further, the action plan builds on the assessment and maps out the coming years: school, track, abilities to build, timeline. The assessment fee is then deducted.
bilan.about_p1: An engineer by training, I have taught mathematics and physics for fourteen years, to students in France and around the world.
bilan.about_p2: I guide international families through their children's education: choosing schools, subject and career choices, selective admissions. The assessment tests are the ones I use with them, aligned with curricula and school requirements.
bilan.f1_a: From Year 4 (CE2) to the final year of secondary school. Tests are adapted to your child's class and curriculum, French, international or British.
bilan.f2_q: Should they prepare for the tests?
bilan.f2_a: No. The tests measure their actual level. Preparing would distort the answer you are looking for.
bilan.f3_a: About a week between your questionnaire answers and the written report, depending on when they take the tests.
bilan.f4_q: How much does the assessment cost?
bilan.f4_a: The fee is given in reply to your first message. If an action plan follows, it is deducted.
bilan.f5_a: Only you. Nothing is shared with their school, and no family is ever named.
bilan.final_sub: A few lines are enough: their age, class, school, what concerns you. I will reply personally.
bilan.final_l1: Tests suited to their age and curriculum
bilan.final_l3: Deducted from the action plan if you continue
